Visual Brand Guide

Colors, typography, spacing, imagery and UI style — for the Host Playbook, future ebooks and social content. Visual reference only; not a content or messaging guide.

1Color palette

Coral is the one accent — used sparingly for CTAs, links and small highlights. The base stays neutral (white / off-white / charcoal) so the accent stands out. Don't introduce new brand colors.

3Logo & icon mark

Two concentric circles, coral stroke — pairs with the "First Look Photo" wordmark (charcoal + coral, Bold). Keep clear space around the icon roughly equal to its own radius. Never recolor, outline or add shadows to it.

Full lockup — light background
Icon only — for avatars / favicons
Icon on dark backgrounds (white ring)

Primary CTA
Secondary / outline
Ghost (on photos)
  • Buttons are always fully pill-shaped (999px radius), bold label text.
  • Numbered badges (e.g. step 1, 2, 3): solid coral circle, ~32px, white bold number.
  • List markers: coral checkmark (✓) for benefits/checklists, coral em-dash (—) for credentials.

6Photography & imagery style

Every photo in the Playbook or social content should match this look — the site's own portfolio is the best reference.

  • Light: bright, naturally lit, true-to-life color — never HDR or over-saturated.
  • Palette in-photo: whites, warm wood, soft grey/beige, one natural accent.
  • Framing: wide but realistic, level horizons, no fisheye, tidy staging.
  • Subjects: interiors, exteriors, decks — often with a view.
  • Aspect ratios: 4:3 for grids/tiles, ~2:1 wide for hero banners.
  • Editing: natural correction only — AI-assisted enhancement should stay photo-realistic.

7Aesthetic, in one line

Clean, warm, uncluttered, editorial-but-approachable — Airbnb-inspired in structure without copying Airbnb's branding — mobile-first, generous whitespace, one accent color used sparingly, calm and trustworthy rather than loud.

8Quick do / don't

DoDon't
Use coral only as an accent, never a background washIntroduce new brand colors beyond the palette
Keep typography to Poppins (or the documented fallback)Use serif, script or condensed/techy fonts
Keep corners rounded — pill buttons, soft card radiiAdd heavy drop shadows or skeuomorphic effects
Use real, bright, naturally-lit property photographyUse over-saturated, HDR or heavily filtered photos
Leave generous whitespace between elementsCrowd a layout — keep one clear focal point per page
